clue.text: Soft pile worn in study is laid down again

indicators.note: 'worn in' places the soft pile inside the word for study

parts.note: to read is to study
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: a pile that is worn is roughed up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A threadbare carpet in someone's study is being relaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft pile' suggests carpet, but soft is just the letter P, and 'worn' makes PLIE of the pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint or plaster that is applied again has been put on a surface a second time.

clue.text: Jumper with jazzy beret? Sparkling stuff

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is an animal that jumps

indicators.note: jazzy means flashy and jumbled, so the letters of beret are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kangaroo in a snazzy beret makes a sparkling sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater; it is the kangaroo. 'jazzy' gives TBEER.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy sweet soft drink flavoured with roots is a sparkling beverage.

clue.text: Within a year, US college shows understanding

indicators.note: 'Within' puts the college inside the letters of a year

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Within a year, an American college demonstrates good relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations between parties, an understanding or concord between them.

clue.text: The work yet to come from PL for truly harmon-ious movement

definitions.text: The work yet to come from PL
definitions.meaning: verse the Poet Laureate (PL) is still working on is in progress, still moving along
the idiom for graceful, beautifully flowing movement

explanation.surface: A poet laureate's unfinished verse is compared to graceful movement.
explanation.walkthrough: PL stands for Poet Laureate, the official national poet in Britain; the hyphen in 'harmon-ious' is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something moving with grace and fluency, like verse made physical.

clue.text: It includes silly positions in a set of runners

parts.note: the field is the set of competitors in a race

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders in silly positions are among a group of runners.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'silly' fielding positions such as silly mid-on are very close to the batsman, so they lie in the infield.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a cricket ground near the wicket contains the silly fielding positions.

clue.text: CID star moves, having a far-reaching effect

indicators.note: when the letters move about they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A star detective of the CID is transferred, with sweeping consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme ones whose effects reach widely.

clue.text: The instant when Jack leaves is uncertain

indicators.note: 'leaves' means the letter for Jack departs from the word for an instant

parts.note: a jiffy is an instant
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: The moment when Jack walks out remains doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iffy is doubtful, full of ifs, so uncertain.

clue.text: This involves items for a dip, of course

definitions.text: This involves items for a dip, of course

parts.words: This involves items for a dip, of course
parts.note: a set of utensils for dipping bread into melted cheese at a meal course; 'of course' also passes as 'naturally'

explanation.surface: A set of things for a swim, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: This set of pot and long forks is what diners use for dipping into melted cheese.

clue.text: Barker looks up the answer about the East

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'looks up' reads the whole construction from bottom to top
'about' puts the reply around the letter for the East

parts.note: a reply is an answer
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A dog-barker consults the solution regarding the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets E inside REPLY to give REPLEY, which 'looks up' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that yelps is giving short sharp barks, so a yelper is a barker.

clue.text: The one with top marks is the main one in the argument

parts.note: the senior one is the chief or main one
a wrangler is someone who argues or disputes

explanation.surface: The top scorer is said to be the chief participant in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge University the student with the highest first-class marks in the mathematics finals was the Senior Wrangler.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cambridge title went to the top-ranked mathematics graduate of the year.

clue.text: Judge work in English

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Assess a piece of work written in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, which is to judge or reckon.

clue.text: Scab found in plant? Alas, not as friendly!

indicators.note: 'found in' puts the strikebreaker inside the plant

parts.note: a fern is a plant
a rat, like a scab, is a strikebreaker or traitor

indicators.note: 'not as' removes the word as from alas

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker turns up among workers, sadly hardly comradely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scab' and 'plant' both hint at strikes and factories; a plant here is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal means brotherly, hence friendly and comradely.

clue.text: A leafy plant, yet bare when treated

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shrub that is leafy, though bare once it has been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay is a laurel shrub or tree grown for its aromatic leaves.

clue.text: Group gathering around peacekeepers' champion

indicators.note: the group gathers round, holding the peacekeepers inside

parts.note: a tribe is a group of people
UN, the United Nations, provides peacekeepers

explanation.surface: A crowd assembles about the defender of UN troops.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a tribune was an official who defended the people, a champion of their rights.

clue.text: It gives the side elevation

parts.note: read not as an architect's drawing but as what lifts a team's morale

explanation.surface: An architectural drawing of a building's flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the shared morale that raises a group's mood.

clue.text: Freedom to hit out? No good for pawn

parts.note: play is freedom of movement, as in a loose rope

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of hit are rearranged

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for no (as in No for number)

explanation.surface: A batsman is given licence to hit out, and is a pawn no use to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit out' reads as a batsman's swing, but 'out' scrambles the letters of hit into THI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is someone used by others, a mere toy in their hands.

clue.text: They show timidity about the doubles

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
ringers, as in dead ringers, are lookalikes or doubles

explanation.surface: People nervous about lookalikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who cringe shrink back in fear, showing timidity.

clue.text: New artist inserted in ad by inferior manager

indicators.note: the new letters are placed inside the ad and its neighbour

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, taken as written
minor means lesser, inferior

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new artist is cast in an advertisement by a junior manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives ISTRAT; 'inferior' is MINOR, and 'by' just sets it beside AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator runs an organisation's affairs, so is a manager.

clue.text: Hurry up to tell what hospitals rely on

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' reads the word for hurry from bottom to top

parts.note: to run is to hurry
to sing is criminal slang for tell, to inform

explanation.surface: Rush to report what hospitals depend upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing, the care of patients, is a service hospitals depend on.

clue.text: Society to press on for what hospitals rely on

parts.note: to urge on is to press on or encourage

explanation.surface: A society urges perseverance for what hospitals need.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates, one of the people hospitals depend on.

clue.text: Row up in sales — a car fault is discovered

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' reads the run from bottom to top
the run is found within the words sales, a, car, fault

explanation.surface: Trouble at the showroom: a car's defect comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'sales a car fault' sits SACARF; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, a row.

clue.text: It goes round both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that turns in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates, turning round on an axis.

clue.text: Criticise the summary

explanation.surface: Find fault with the précis.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down is to disparage, and a rundown is a quick summary of the facts.

clue.text: Better or worst?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to better is to surpass
as a verb, to worst is to defeat

explanation.surface: Is it better or worse?
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, so both verbs, to better and to worst, mean the same.

clue.text: Fabric made with inner coil

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A material produced with an internal spiral.
explanation.walkthrough: Crinoline was originally a stiff fabric of horsehair and linen before it named the hooped petticoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Crinoline is a stiff fabric used to stiffen skirts.

clue.text: River obstruction fixed by explosive

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A blockage on the river is cleared by blasting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethe is a river of Hades in Greek myth.

clue.text: Herb has no time for the theatre

indicators.note: 'has no' means the letter for time is absent from the word

parts.note: the stage is the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: Herb, an actor, cannot find time for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an aromatic culinary herb.

clue.text: Very large room using design

indicators.note: the letters are designed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A very big room is used for design work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginormous is slang for huge, a blend of gigantic and enormous.
